views.name: tracks_with_context
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId,
  t.Name,
  t.AlbumId,
  a.Title AS Title,
  a.ArtistId,
  ar.Name AS Name /* Artist Name */,
  t.MediaTypeId,
  mt.Name AS Name /* MediaType Name */,
  t.GenreId,
  g.Name AS Name /* Genre Name */,
  t.Composer,
  t.Milliseconds,
  t.Bytes,
  t.UnitPrice
FROM tracks t
LEFT JOIN albums a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ar ON a.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
LEFT JOIN media_types mt ON t.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId
views.description: One row per track enriched with album, artist, genre, and media type attributes. Use this when you need track-level details together with their album/artist/dimension labels for reporting, filtering, or joins to sales/playlists. | Use for: List tracks with their album and artist names; Filter tracks by genre or media type and return composer/duration; Join track details to sales/playlist data for aggregation

views.name: invoice_items_with_track_and_invoice
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId,
  inv.InvoiceDate,
  inv.BillingCountry,
  ii.TrackId,
  t.Name AS Name /* Track Name */,
  t.AlbumId,
  a.Title AS Title,
  a.ArtistId,
  ar.Name AS Name /* Artist Name */,
  ii.UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity
FROM invoice_items ii
JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ar ON a.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
views.description: One row per invoice line item enriched with its parent invoice and track details (including track name, album, artist, and invoice header fields). Use for sales analysis at line-item grain, attribution to customers, and joining to track metadata. | Use for: Compute revenue by track/artist/genre/customer; List invoice lines with customer and track metadata; Filter sales by billing country or invoice date and attribute to tracks/artists

views.name: customer_invoice_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inv.CustomerId,
  COUNT(inv.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count,
  SUM(inv.Total) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(inv.Total) AS avg_invoice_value,
  MAX(inv.InvoiceDate) AS last_invoice_date
FROM invoices inv
GROUP BY inv.CustomerId
views.description: Aggregated invoice-level metrics per customer: number of invoices, total revenue, average invoice value, and most recent invoice date. Use this for customer lifetime value, segmentation, and recency-based cohorts. | Use for: Rank customers by total revenue or number of purchases; Segment customers by recency/frequency/monetary (RFM); Identify customers with no recent invoices (using last_invoice_date)

views.name: track_sales_aggregate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ii.TrackId,
  SUM(ii.Quantity) AS total_quantity_sold,
  SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ii.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count,
  MIN(inv.InvoiceDate) AS first_sale_date,
  MAX(inv.InvoiceDate) AS last_sale_date
FROM invoice_items ii
JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
GROUP BY ii.TrackId
views.description: Sales aggregated at the track level: total quantity sold, total revenue, number of distinct invoices, and first/last sale date. Use to identify best-selling tracks and temporal sales trends per track. | Use for: Find top-selling tracks by quantity or revenue; Measure sales lifecycle for a track (first/last sale); Join to track metadata to report artist/album sales

views.name: customer_full_contact
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.CustomerId,
  c.FirstName,
  c.LastName,
  c.Company,
  c.Address,
  c.City,
  c.State,
  c.Country,
  c.PostalCode,
  c.Phone,
  c.Fax,
  c.Email,
  c.SupportRepId
FROM customers c
views.description: One row per customer projecting canonical contact fields and support rep association. Useful when building customer lists, joining to sales, or mapping customers to employees (support reps). | Use for: List customers with contact details and their support representative; Filter customers by country/city for marketing lists; Join customer contacts to invoices/orders

views.name: employee_hierarchy_paths
views.body_sql:
SELECT e.EmployeeId AS EmployeeId, e.ReportsTo AS ManagerId, 0 AS depth
FROM employees e
WHERE e.EmployeeId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Management reporting paths: all ancestor chains for employees (employee -> manager -> manager ...). One row per (EmployeeId, ManagerId_ancestor) pair with depth. Use for org reporting, computing chain-of-command or aggregating team metrics up the hierarchy. | Use for: Compute aggregates rolled up to managers (join this to sales/employees); Show full management chain for a given employee; Count reports at each managerial level

views.name: playlist_track_with_metadata
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.PlaylistId,
  pl.Name AS Name /* Playlist Name */,
  pt.TrackId,
  t.Name AS Name /* Track Name */,
  t.AlbumId,
  a.Title AS Title,
  a.ArtistId,
  ar.Name AS Name /* Artist Name */,
  t.GenreId,
  g.Name AS Name /* Genre Name */,
  t.Milliseconds,
  t.UnitPrice
FROM playlist_track pt
LEFT JOIN playlists pl ON pt.PlaylistId = pl.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums a ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ar ON a.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
views.description: One row per playlist membership enriched with track, album, and artist metadata. Useful for playlist analysis, finding popular tracks across playlists, or exporting playlist content with full context. | Use for: List all tracks in a playlist with artist and album info; Find tracks that appear in many playlists; Analyze average track length/price within playlists

views.name: tracks_duration_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId,
  t.GenreId,
  t.Milliseconds,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.GenreId ORDER BY t.Milliseconds DESC) AS duration_rank
FROM tracks t
views.description: Per-genre ranking of tracks by duration (Milliseconds). Exposes a rank so callers can filter for top-N per genre downstream. Use to identify longest/shortest tracks within each genre. | Use for: Select top-N longest tracks per genre (WHERE duration_rank <= N); Compare duration distributions by genre; Find shortest tracks (ORDER BY duration_rank ASC or WHERE duration_rank = 1)
